a.basis: India coal-thermal fleet average, operational (combustion) intensity — India's older, less-efficient coal fleet sits toward the upper end of global coal-plant ranges (~0.85-1.05 kg/kWh).

c.basis: Gas (combined-cycle) generation, operational intensity — roughly half of coal's per-kWh footprint, consistent with typical global gas-CCGT figures (~0.40-0.49 kg/kWh).

d.basis: Lifecycle intensity (construction, reservoir methane where applicable) — hydro has near-zero operational emissions but a small lifecycle footprint is commonly included.

e.basis: Lifecycle intensity (turbine/tower manufacture, foundation) — no operational combustion emissions.

f.basis: Lifecycle intensity (panel manufacture is the dominant contributor) — no operational combustion emissions.

g.basis: Lifecycle intensity (fuel cycle, plant construction) — no operational combustion emissions.

Stainless steel is a passive structural/equipment material — it does not consume energy or emit GHGs during its use phase (unlike, say, a sold vehicle or appliance). Generally reported as zero/not applicable unless the product is an energy-using finished good, which is out of scope for a steelmaker selling coil/plate/bar.

downstream.category: Cat. 12 — End-of-Life Treatment of Sold Products
downstream.notes: (a) Emissions FROM disposal/recycling processing of the product once scrapped — typically small (mechanical shredding/baling energy) versus production-phase emissions. (b) The separate, commonly-discussed 'circularity credit': stainless steel's high end-of-life recycling rate (India: material substantially recovered back into scrap streams, often cited >85-90% recovery for structural stainless) means a large share of the virgin-route carbon burden is avoided in the NEXT product life cycle — but this avoided-emissions claim is accounted for as a benefit to whichever future product uses that recycled scrap (i.e., it shows up as the low-carbon 'y' scrap-route coefficients used throughout the main grid), not as a credit within this product's own Category 12. Do not double-count it here.
